institutionName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Location of the university and how the academics were on that university. 
Another thing I thought about was the possibilities of social gatherings

questions.answer: Not very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different kinds of dorm rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only meal plans where I was living

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Even though the housing website says that there is a kitchen there is none. We had the get the meal plan to eat

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was difficult because once we got the chance to apply for housing it was a long timne after other students got the chance so all the better housing options were already taken

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Once we got access to registration process we could look for all the courses that were being offered to us. A bit of a mess with all the different departments and such.
After we found a course we would like to enroll in we had to write an email to the professor of that course and explain that you were a exchange student and would like to enroll in that class. You had to attach a file with the necessary prerequisites that you had had at my home university.
This took a long time and in the meantime some of the courses got filled so I could not enroll because the professor was slow to answer.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could write to the exchange office but they did were not a lot of help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that successful. Out of all the courses I was interested in I only got two of them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apparently, a lot of the courses that were filled will before the start of the semester will become avaliable on and off during the first week of classes. If you really want a specific class be on ConnectCarolina and refresh the enrollment site many times and hope that your specific course gets avaliable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am on my last year on my BA and had course levels between 100 and 600.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were a lot more self studies compared to UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I expected to be ably to cook my own food because the housing website stated that there were a kitchen. However there werent so I had to pay for the more expensive meal plan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: General food were more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I was really satisfied with the non-academic opportunities. 
But, for some reason I couldnt enroll in the lotteries for the home football games. I asked the exchange office and they said that only full time students and student athleats could enter the lottery. However some of my friends who were from CBS could enter the lottery without any problems.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot of religious and cultural studies. 
And also plenty of athletic opporunities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the sports games

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is not a lot to see around the university but I would recommend going of as many trips as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The ony problems I had was how to adress your teachers with sir or mam and niit their first name. Otherwise, there werent any problems adjusting

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go out and socialize at night
And be friendly during classes so you will get to know a few from each class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everybody was really friendly and talkative. The Southern Charm as they say.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be prepared and start looking for housing and courses early
- Depending on how old you are be prepared for people being a lot younger when they start at university than when people in Denmark start at the university
- I will be more expensive that you'll think

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: - A introduction and orientation when you arrive would be very usefull

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cutural rewards were the best part

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: becomming real friends with the americans.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I recommend joining a sport club (if you are interested)
A great way to get to know people.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
